actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

facts.text: robopal is a robot simulation framework on the MuJoCo physics engine
The framework offers Gymnasium style single-arm and PettingZoo style bimanual environments
The model integrates with a timestep of 0.0005 s, the implicitfast integrator and gravity -9.81 m/s^2
The seven motors a1..a7 command those joints and their ctrlrange is -80.0 to 80.0
The arm geoms are visual only (contype 0, conaffinity 0) except the collision geom of the last link, so the template model has almost no contacts
The DrawerCubeEnv manipulation environment builds its robot from the DianaDrawerCube class by default
DianaDrawerCube derives from DianaMed, the robot class whose manipulator is the DianaMed template
A robot class splices its manipulator, gripper and scene into one MJCF model with RobotGenerator and saves that model for the environment
In a spliced scene the arm joints and actuators are prefixed (0_j1..0_j7, 0_a1..0_a7)
The DrawerCubeEnv environment runs at a control frequency of 20 Hz with the CARTIK controller and limits an episode to 50 steps

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the model deterministically from the reset state; the model has no random element, so the same ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder dynamics are not the model's.

gaps: the model is the DianaMed manipulator template only: the gripper, task objects (drawer, cube), the spliced scene, the reward, the goal and the 50-step episode limit of the environment are not served
rigid-body dynamics of the seven-joint arm with the model's inertias, damping, joint ranges and motor ctrlranges; the arm geoms are visual only, so contacts are negligible in the template
no rendering, no sensors, no cameras and no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 0.0005 s step only

the fake backend is not MuJoCo: it reads the model's timestep, joint count and actuator ctrlranges from the model file, then integrates a placeholder model (ctrl drives qvel, qvel drives qpos) with no inertias, contacts, constraints or actuators of the real solver; its trajectories are not valid simulation results
the joint ranges of the model file bound qpos in MuJoCo; the fake does not enforce them (the runtime's only limit is the actuator ctrlrange the bridge derives)

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the model state is kept and stays readable
